title: Rhododendrons of Sikkim: species, places, months
meta_description: Sikkim's rhododendrons explained: how many species, which to look for, and where and when they flower at Barsey, Yumthang and Shingba, with sources.
summary: Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills hold 45 rhododendron taxa, including 36 species, according to the Botanical Survey of India's 2022 account. They flower from late February in the lower hills to June in the alpine meadows. The best places to see them are the Barsey sanctuary in late March and April and Yumthang and Shingba in May.

sections.heading: Why Sikkim and rhododendrons go together
paras: Few plants are as tied to a place as the rhododendron is to Sikkim. The state tree is Rhododendron niveum, a species with lilac-purple flowers that grows at about 2,600–3,500 m, and the state has two sanctuaries named for the genus: Barsey in Soreng district and Shingba in Mangan district (North Sikkim). In spring whole hillsides turn red, pink, white and yellow, and rhododendron season brings more domestic visitors to some corners of the state than any festival.

The scientific story begins with the botanist Joseph Dalton Hooker, who travelled in Sikkim in 1848 and 1849. His book The Rhododendrons of Sikkim-Himalaya, published in parts from 1849 to 1851 with plates drawn by Walter Hood Fitch from Hooker's field sketches, introduced many of these species to Western science and to British gardens. Later explorers relied on Sikkimese collectors. The Botanical Survey of India's 2022 book Rhododendrons of Sikkim and Darjeeling Himalaya is dedicated to two of them, Rhomoo Lepcha and Ribu Lepcha, who collected plants for botanists in the early 20th century, including on the 1909–10 expeditions led by William Wright Smith and George Cave.

sections.heading: How many species are there
paras: The most recent count comes from that 2022 book by Rajib Gogoi, Norbu Sherpa, Ashiho A. Mao, Samuel Rai and Subrata Gupta, published by the Botanical Survey of India with West Bengal's Directorate of Cinchona and Other Medicinal Plants. It describes 45 rhododendron taxa in Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills: 36 species, one subspecies, one variety and seven natural hybrids. An earlier standard work, Sikkim-Himalayan Rhododendrons by U. C. Pradhan and S. T. Lachungpa (1990), also recorded 36 species for Sikkim.

The count keeps shifting as botanists work through remote valleys. Species described from Sikkim in recent decades include R. sikkimense, named by Pradhan and Lachungpa, and others described since 2014. New populations of the state tree itself were reported inside Khangchendzonga National Park in 2010. Natural hybrids form where two species grow together; the BSI book illustrates one between R. aeruginosum and R. wightii from the alpine slopes at Yumesamdong (Zero Point).

sections.heading: Species worth learning to recognise
paras: You do not need to be a botanist to tell a few apart. The details below come from the BSI's 2022 account unless noted; flowering months shift with altitude and weather. Nepali names are widely used in the villages: gurans and chimal both mean rhododendron, with gurans usually used for the tree forms.

sections.heading: Barsey: the south-west in March and April
paras: The Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary covers about 104 sq km of the Singalila Range in Soreng district, from about 2,200 m to 4,100 m. Most visitors walk the 4 km trail from Hilley (about 2,730 m) to the Barsey clearing (about 3,000 m), through rhododendron, oak and magnolia forest. Because it sits lower and further south than the North Sikkim sanctuaries, it flowers earlier. Tree rhododendrons colour the slopes around Okhrey from late February, and the trail from Hilley is usually at its best from the last week of March to the last week of April.

The BSI book records Lady Dalhousie's rhododendron at Barsey, a large, scented, pale-flowered species often growing on rocks or other trees, and notes that the red form of R. cinnabarinum is common along the Singalila ridge. Indians need no permit; foreigners need only Sikkim's Restricted Area Permit. A forest entry fee is collected at Hilley; check current status before you travel. Our Hilley to Barsey guide covers the walk in detail.

sections.heading: Yumthang and Shingba: the north in May
paras: In North Sikkim the season comes later. Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary, notified in 1984, lies in the Yumthang valley north of Lachung, at around 3,500 m, and the valley floor and slopes are usually in flower from late April through May. R. cinnabarinum is recorded at both Shingba and Yumthang in the BSI account. Higher up, towards Yumesamdong (Zero Point), dwarf alpine rhododendrons flower in late May and June among primulas and other alpine plants.

Getting there is a bigger undertaking than Barsey. Yumthang needs a protected-area permit arranged through a Sikkim Tourism-registered agent, operators require a minimum two-night stay in North Sikkim, and children under five are not permitted in the protected areas. Foreign nationals can visit Lachung, Yumthang and Zero Point with a protected-area permit in a group of two or more. Roads in the north close after landslides and snow, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Planning a rhododendron trip
paras: Because the flowering climbs with altitude, you can follow it across the state. A trip in the first three weeks of April catches Barsey at its best; a trip in mid-May catches Yumthang and Shingba. Very few visitors manage both peaks in one go, but a two-week trip from about 10 April to 25 April can see the end of Barsey and the start of the higher forests around Lachung, though Yumthang may not yet be in full colour.

For Barsey, sleep in Okhrey, about 10 km below Hilley, for two nights, and walk to Barsey on the clearest morning. Add Rinchenpong and Kaluk, about 2.5 hours away, for the Kangchenjunga views, or Pelling and Yuksom if you want monasteries and the start of the Dzongri trail. For Yumthang, base yourself in Lachung for two nights on a North Sikkim package from Gangtok, with permits arranged by a registered agent.

Bloom dates are never certain. A warm, dry March can bring Barsey forward; a late snowfall can hold Yumthang back into June. We ask homestays and drivers on the ground for a bloom report a week or two before each departure, and we suggest keeping a spare day in any rhododendron itinerary in case of rain or cloud.

sections.heading: Looking without harming
paras: Rhododendrons are protected in the sanctuaries, and picking flowers or breaking branches is prohibited. Outside them, many villages still value the plants: dried leaves of the small alpine R. anthopogon are burnt as incense, which is where its Nepali name dhupi comes from, and the wood of larger species was used for fuel and tools. Overgrazing and firewood cutting once damaged parts of Barsey; a paper in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh's journal Sibbaldia credits the sanctuary's grazing controls and community eco-development committees with helping the forest regenerate.

Some rhododendron flowers and honey made from them can be toxic if eaten, so do not taste flowers on the trail. Stay on paths, take photographs rather than flowers, and leave the forest as you found it.
list: Visit early in the morning, before cloud and crowds
Use a zoom lens rather than pulling branches closer
Note altitude and date with your photographs; it helps identification
Carry a refillable bottle and bring all rubbish back

faqs.q: How many rhododendron species are found in Sikkim?
faqs.a: The Botanical Survey of India's 2022 book Rhododendrons of Sikkim and Darjeeling Himalaya describes 45 taxa in Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills: 36 species, one subspecies, one variety and seven natural hybrids. Pradhan and Lachungpa's 1990 book also recorded 36 species for Sikkim. New species and new populations are still being described, so the number may change.

faqs.q: What is the state tree of Sikkim?
faqs.a: Rhododendron niveum is Sikkim's state tree. It has rounded clusters of lilac-purple flowers and leaves with a pale, felted underside, and grows at about 2,600–3,500 m in Sikkim, Bhutan and southern Tibet. It is uncommon, and new populations were reported inside Khangchendzonga National Park in 2010, which was welcome news for its conservation.

faqs.q: When do rhododendrons bloom in Sikkim?
faqs.a: From late February to June, rising with altitude. Tree rhododendrons flower first in the lower hills in late February and March. Barsey in Soreng district usually peaks from the last week of March to the last week of April. Yumthang and Shingba in North Sikkim peak from late April through May, and alpine species near Zero Point flower in late May and June.

faqs.q: Which is better for rhododendrons, Barsey or Yumthang?
faqs.a: Both are excellent but different. Barsey flowers earlier, needs no special permit for Indians and is an easy 4 km forest walk from Hilley. Yumthang flowers later, in May, in an open high valley with snow peaks around, but needs a protected-area permit, a two-night minimum North Sikkim trip and is not allowed for children under five.

Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary lies in the Yumthang valley north of Lachung in Mangan district (North Sikkim), at around 3,500 m. It was notified in 1984. Visitors see it on the drive from Lachung to Yumthang, which needs a protected-area permit through a registered agent. The best flowering is usually late April to May; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Who was Joseph Hooker and why does he matter for Sikkim?
faqs.a: Joseph Dalton Hooker was a British botanist who travelled through Sikkim in 1848 and 1849. His book The Rhododendrons of Sikkim-Himalaya, published from 1849 to 1851 with plates by Walter Hood Fitch, introduced many Sikkim rhododendrons to Western science and gardens. Several species, such as R. dalhousieae and R. thomsonii, carry names he gave them.

faqs.q: Can I pick rhododendron flowers in Sikkim?
faqs.a: No, not in the sanctuaries, where picking flowers or breaking branches is prohibited and forest staff check bags at busy times. Elsewhere, please leave them too: rhododendron forests are slow-growing and already under pressure. Some rhododendron flowers and honey can also be toxic if eaten. Take photographs instead, ideally with a zoom lens.

Lali Gurans is the Nepali name for Rhododendron arboreum, the tree rhododendron, which has bright scarlet to pink flowers and is one of the first to bloom each year in the lower and middle hills. It is the national flower of Nepal and is common across Sikkim's temperate forests, including the slopes around Okhrey below Barsey.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to see rhododendrons in Sikkim?
faqs.a: It depends where. Barsey in Soreng district needs no special permit for Indians, only a forest entry fee at Hilley. Yumthang, Shingba, Zero Point and Kyongnosla are in protected areas and need permits through a registered agent. The Dzongri trail needs a trekking permit. Foreign nationals need Sikkim's Restricted Area Permit everywhere. Check current status before you travel.
